reflection.quote: We are what we repeatedly do. Excellence, then, is not an act, but a habit.
reflection.reading:
Sunday in late October has a particular quality to it. The light is thinner, the leaves are mostly down, and there's a kind of permission in the air to do very little. When I was drinking, Sundays were for damage assessment — piecing together the night before, bracing for Monday, chasing the hangover with whatever was left in the fridge. The day didn't belong to me. It belonged to the mess.

What I didn't understand at 22 was that a quiet Sunday isn't a smaller life. It's the actual thing. It's reading a book until your coffee goes cold. It's calling your mom back. It's folding laundry while something plays in the background. It's the walk you take because your body wants to move, not because you're trying to sweat out poison. These are the hours that stack up into a life you recognize as your own.

Durant's line about habit lands here. The person I am today wasn't built in the big moments — the ski trips, the jumps out of planes, the hunts. Those are the dividends. The principal is the ordinary Sunday, done sober, done again next week, done again the week after. Showing up for the small, unremarkable hours is how you become someone you can actually live with.
reflection.meditation: Today, let the quiet count. Nothing has to happen for this day to matter.

affirmations: I am building a life out of ordinary days done well.
Today I don't owe anyone a performance — I just have to show up sober.
I am becoming someone I can live with, one honest hour at a time.

gratitude.prayer: Grateful for a Sunday that belongs to me — no reconstruction, no apologies owed, no wreckage to clean. Grateful for the kind of light that comes through the window in October, and for the fact that I'm awake to see it. Grateful for the people who stuck around while I figured out how to stick around for myself. And grateful, still, for the day I ran out of other options and had to try something different.
gratitude.closing: One more day. That's the whole thing.
